prompt: Of the 1000 rows, how many did the `LazyColumn` compose in the test?
hint: 640 dp of screen, 48 dp a row.

prompt: A `Column` with `verticalScroll` holds 500 sessions. What does it compose when the screen opens?
hint: Scrolling does not make it lazy.

choices.text: All 500
choices.why: Right: a `Column` composes every child, on screen or not.

choices.text: The ones on screen, plus one page ahead
choices.why: That describes a lazy list; the scroll modifier does not change what a `Column` composes.

choices.text: Only the first, until the user scrolls
choices.why: Nothing is deferred in a `Column`.

choices.text: None, until layout measures the screen
choices.why: Composition comes before layout, and a `Column` composes them all.

prompt: What is the lambda in `items(1000) { i -> … }`?
hint: It is not a loop body.

choices.text: A loop body run a thousand times at once
choices.why: The count printed fourteen, not a thousand.

choices.text: A recipe for one row, called on demand
choices.why: Right: the list calls it on demand, as rows come on screen.

choices.text: A callback run after all items are laid out
choices.why: It produces the rows; nothing is laid out before it runs.

choices.text: A filter that decides which items to keep
choices.why: Every index is kept; the lambda draws one.

prompt: Without keys, a student opens session 10 at the top, then session 9 is inserted above it. Which session shows its details?

choices.text: Session 10, which was tapped
choices.why: That is what keys give you; without them the state stays at position 0.

choices.text: Session 9
choices.why: Right: it moved into position 0, where the open state stayed.

choices.text: Neither, because the insert resets all state
choices.why: Inserting resets nothing; the state stayed at its position.

choices.text: Both, because state is copied to the new row
choices.why: State is never copied; one row holds it.

prompt: Which is the right key for the planner's session rows?

choices.text: The index in the list
choices.why: That is what no key means already.

choices.text: The course name
choices.why: Several sessions share a course, and keys must be unique.

choices.text: The session's `id`
choices.why: Right: unique, unchanging, and a `Long` fits in a `Bundle`.

choices.text: The date and the minutes, joined
choices.why: Two sessions can share both, and editing the minutes would change the key.

prompt: A list uses `LocalDateTime` objects as keys and builds fine. What does the lesson say a key on Android must also be?
hint: The scroll position may have to survive the process.

choices.text: Of a type a `Bundle` can hold
choices.why: Right: `Long`, `Int` and `String` all qualify, which is why the headers use `date.toString()`.

choices.text: Sorted, so the list can search it
choices.why: Keys need no order.

choices.text: Shorter than 64 characters
choices.why: No length rule was given.

choices.text: A `String`, and nothing else
choices.why: The sessions use a `Long` id.

prompt: To make state follow the item, write `items(sessions, ___ = { it.id }) { SessionItem(it) }`.
What does `stickyHeader` add over a plain `item`?

choices.text: It stays pinned at the top
choices.why: Right: Thursday's header stayed on top, drawn over session 11.

choices.text: It is composed before every other item
choices.why: It is composed lazily like the rest.

choices.text: It cannot scroll at all
choices.why: It scrolls away when the next header pushes it.

choices.text: It needs no key
choices.why: The planner gives it one, the date as a `String`.

prompt: What does `contentType` let the list do?

choices.text: Sort the items by type
choices.why: Order comes from the calls; `contentType` does not reorder.

choices.text: Reuse rows between alike items
choices.why: Right: a header is reused for a header and a session row for a session.

choices.text: Skip composing headers
choices.why: Headers were composed and drawn.

choices.text: Give each type its own scroll position
choices.why: There is one `LazyListState` for the list.

prompt: Why are the day names in the screenshot English even though the app might run on a Portuguese phone?

choices.text: Robolectric only speaks English
choices.why: The locale is fixed in the code, not by Robolectric.

choices.text: `strings.xml` has no `values-pt`
choices.why: The day names do not come from `strings.xml` at all.

choices.text: The formatter was built with `Locale.ENGLISH`
choices.why: Right: a real app formats dates in the user's locale.

choices.text: `LocalDate` stores the name of the day
choices.why: It stores a date; the name comes from formatting.

prompt: Thirty sessions, three a day, one header per day. How many items does the list hold in total?
After scrolling to item 14, the first key laid out was `2026-10-29`, whose index is 12. Why is item 12 on screen when the first visible item is 14?

choices.text: The sticky header is pinned and drawn over item 14
choices.why: Right: that is what `stickyHeader` does.

choices.text: `performScrollToIndex` stops two items short
choices.why: The state says item 14 is first, offset 0.

choices.text: The list keeps two items above as a buffer
choices.why: The only item before 14 in the list is the header.

choices.text: Indexes count only sessions, not headers
choices.why: They count everything the list emitted; total was 40.

prompt: A button should appear once the list has left its first item. Why wrap the check in `derivedStateOf`?

choices.text: So it recomposes only when the answer flips
choices.why: Right: lesson 5 explains why it works.

choices.text: Because `firstVisibleItemIndex` can only be read inside it
choices.why: It can be read anywhere; reading it directly recomposes more often.

choices.text: To run the check on a background thread
choices.why: Nothing moves threads here.

choices.text: To save the answer across rotation
choices.why: That would be `rememberSaveable`, lesson 4.

prompt: Why does `SessionList` take a `LazyListState` parameter with a default?

choices.text: So it works alone, or with a caller's own state
choices.why: Right: the test passed its own to read the scroll.

choices.text: Because a `LazyColumn` cannot create its own state
choices.why: The default creates one with `rememberLazyListState()`.

choices.text: To share one scroll position between all lists in the app
choices.why: Each call gets its own unless one is passed.

choices.text: It is required by `stickyHeader`
choices.why: Sticky headers work with any state.

prompt: Without `totalItemsCount > 0`, the list loaded a second page before anybody scrolled. Why?
hint: What does the layout info hold before the first layout?

choices.text: The page size was too small for the screen
choices.why: With the fix, one page of twenty was enough to open with.

choices.text: Before layout, 0 ≥ −5 is true
choices.why: Right: an empty layout looks like a list scrolled to its end.

choices.text: `LaunchedEffect` runs twice on every screen
choices.why: It runs when its key changes; the key was true from the start.

choices.text: Robolectric scrolls the list on its own
choices.why: The first line was printed before any scroll.

prompt: Put what happened in the test in order.
hint: The list asks; the pager answers.
items: the list opens with one page of 20
`nearTheEnd` becomes true and `loadMore` adds a second page
scrolling to item 59 loads nothing, at the total of 60

prompt: Why is `pager.loaded` a `mutableStateOf`?
hint: Who needs to know a page arrived?

choices.text: So the list redraws on a new page
choices.why: Right: the `items` call reads it.

choices.text: So it survives rotation
choices.why: `mutableStateOf` alone does not survive rotation; lesson 4.

choices.text: To make the server call asynchronous
choices.why: There is no server yet, and state does not make anything asynchronous.

choices.text: Because `LazyColumn` only accepts state lists
choices.why: It accepts any `List`; only state makes it update.

prompt: Match each piece of `EndlessList` to its job.

pairs.right: Turns the scroll into one yes or no
Runs `loadMore` when that answer becomes true
Draws what has arrived so far

prompt: Which library does the lesson name as the full answer to paging, with loading and error states?

choices.text: Paging 3
choices.why: Right: it works with `LazyColumn` through `collectAsLazyPagingItems()`.

choices.text: Room
choices.why: Room is the database of lesson 15.

choices.text: WorkManager
choices.why: That runs background work, lesson 18.

choices.text: Coil
choices.why: Coil loads images, lesson 17.

prompt: A list of sessions refreshes from the network and the wrong rows end up expanded. Which changes help? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Add `key = { it.id }` to `items`
choices.why: Yes: state then follows the session.

choices.text: Replace the `LazyColumn` with a `Column`
choices.why: A `Column` also keeps state by position, and composes everything.

choices.text: Make sure the server's ids do not change between refreshes
choices.why: Yes: a key is only as stable as the id behind it.

choices.text: Add `contentType` to every item
choices.why: That affects reuse of compositions, not whose state is whose.

prompt: A tablet shows 30 rows at once and the pager's page is 20. With `EndlessList`'s threshold of five, what happens when the screen opens?
hint: Compare the last visible index with the total minus five.

choices.text: Nothing until the student scrolls
choices.why: All twenty fit on screen, so the last visible one is already near the end.

choices.text: A second page loads at once, before any scroll
choices.why: Right: the last visible index, 19, is already within five of 20; with 40 loaded it no longer is.

choices.text: It crashes, because the page is smaller than the screen
choices.why: A short page is not an error; it only loads more.

choices.text: It loads all sixty and stops paging
choices.why: After the second page, index 29 is not within five of 40, so it waits.
